title: DNAの二重らせん ― ロザリンド・フランクリンの静かな貢献
style: 画風01・光彩のある劇場アニメ背景を基調にした写実的な科学史ドキュメンタリー
research_basis: King's College London: Rosalind Franklin / Photograph 51
NobelPrize.org: 1962 medicine prize and Foundation statutes
timeline: 1951-1953 King's College London: Franklin and Gosling's DNA X-ray diffraction work
January 1953: Wilkins showed the image to Watson without Franklin's knowledge
25 April 1953: three related Nature papers published together
1953 onward: Franklin at Birkbeck working on virus structures
1962: Crick, Watson and Wilkins received the Nobel Prize

rosalind_franklin.identity: pale oval face, dark expressive eyebrows, dark wavy hair swept back with a side part, direct thoughtful eyes
rosalind_franklin.wardrobe: white 1950s lab coat over a restrained charcoal or muted teal blouse; dark skirt; no modern PPE
rosalind_franklin.manner: precise, self-possessed, concentrated; never reduced to a passive victim

raymond_gosling.identity: young British research student, short tidy brown hair, slim build
raymond_gosling.wardrobe: white lab coat, shirt and dark tie

james_watson.identity: young, tall and lean, short side-parted dark hair, clean-shaven
james_watson.wardrobe: brown tweed jacket, white shirt, narrow tie

francis_crick.identity: taller and broader, receding wavy dark hair, strong eyebrows, clean-shaven
francis_crick.wardrobe: dark gray suit, white shirt, tie

maurice_wilkins.identity: tall, slim, thinning dark hair, reserved expression
maurice_wilkins.wardrobe: dark brown or charcoal suit, white shirt, tie

science_accuracy: Photograph 51 is an X-ray diffraction pattern, not a medical X-ray image or a direct photograph of a helix
show thin hydrated DNA fibres, an X-ray camera and photographic film; no modern sequencers or computer displays
the X-shaped pattern supports helical geometry but does not alone visually contain a literal double helix
the 1953 Nature issue contained related papers by Watson-Crick, Wilkins-Stokes-Wilson, and Franklin-Gosling
Franklin's contribution includes rigorous measurements and analysis, not Photograph 51 alone
history_accuracy: Wilkins showing Photograph 51 to Watson is depicted as an understated act in an already strained collaboration, not a theatrical theft scene
Franklin must not be shown alive at the 1962 Nobel ceremony
the Nobel scene includes exactly Crick, Watson and Wilkins as the medicine laureates
the no-posthumous-award point is shown through absence and archival procedure, not a fictional rejected nomination

composition.subtitle_safe_area: keep important faces, hands, film and instruments above the lower 45 percent
composition.camera: one stable push, pull or hold per shot
composition.text: no readable generated labels, signatures, journal titles or equations

avoid: glowing fantasy DNA filling the laboratory
modern computers, LED displays, pipettes or sequencers
lab goggles and disposable nitrile gloves unless historically justified
villainous sneaking, document theft, courtroom imagery or a Nobel jury
Franklin as a ghost at the 1962 ceremony
readable generated text, logos, watermarks or captions inside source images
